Open Space;
The City of Cambridge has adopted a Zoning Ordinance Amendment which creates a new zoning district—Cambridge Center Mixed Use Development (MSD) District— for the presently undeveloped portion of Kendall Square Urban Renewal Area. The controls of this zoning amendment have been incorporated in the Kendall Square Urban Renewal Plan as revised Amendment No. 1. The revised amendment Exhibit "AA" is included in the Final Statement.
The zoning amendment provides for two types of open space requirements. First, a minimum of 100,000 square feet of land within the district must be reserved as public open space. Second, there is an open space requirement for each lot within the district based on the type(s) and amount of use)s) on the lot. The requirement for a lot may be reduced if land is dedicated as public open space or is located next to public open space. The regulations also encourage physical integration of development within the district by allowing a variety of pedestrian ways such as elevated walkways and arcades to be counted as open space.
With reference to "Residential Uses", the regulations provide that a minimum of 15 square feet of open space will be provided for each 100 square feet of gross floor area. The specific activities proposed for the open space will be determined by the Authority's design advisory group which will take into consideration the residents' recreational needs as well as aesthetics in arriving at its determinations.
While it appears that close to the entire 2.5- acre allotment for public open space may be needed for good design of access plazas, etc., it also appears that actually developed public open space will exceed that minimum and that much of the total public open space will be passively recreational in nature.
The suggestions that the final report "completely" document proposed landscape development, establish a critical ratio between paved and landscaped areas, and consider the development of the continuous green-belt on the periphery of the project appear to be inconsistent with the statement, under the aesthetics section of the same letter, that detailed design work cannot yet by presented. Landscaping decisions are appropriately a part of the subsequent design review procedures.
